chapter: Second lining and the brass bands
title: Rabbit Brown, James Alley and a message for Louis
summary: Allen asks about the song on the death of the chief and Rabbit, who sang and played guitar; White bummed around James Alley, sat in on drums at picnics, and sends greetings to Louis.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Do you remember that song they used to have about the downfall of the line, they called it? Yeah. Well... I think Rabbit used to sing it, the guy who played guitar? Yeah. Rabbit singing? Yeah, I know Rabbit.

Used to hang around James Alley? Yeah, I know. I used to bum in James Alley. Oh, you? I used to bum around James Alley. Eclip Alley. Mm-hmm. All around. All around up and down. Where's Eclip Alley? Right on Franklin and Gravy.
Franklin and Gravy. Yeah. You remember, you say you remember Rabbit, huh? Yeah, I remember Rabbit.

Do you remember what he used to sing? I forgot, I forgot not what he used to sing. I know he used to, yeah, I forgot what he used to sing, no. He had some song about that who killed the chief business. What's he? I forgot what kind of song he used to sing so many songs to that day too, that I didn't know what. Half of the time I didn't know what he was singing. Sometime I used to catch Rabbit. Say Rabbit, he say what? Say, you all playing tonight? Say, yeah, man, we playing in such and such a place. Say, alright. Let's call it? Yeah. Well, I get my pass. If you all playing for a picnic, I get a pass to go to picnic. Well, now, all y'all, all y'all, you, you, you, and you all, all y'all be playing and come up there. Say, sometime, sometime your, you say, your drummer get tired playing. He says, I'm going downtown. I'm going, I'm going to dance a little bit. I feel like dancing. They want to go there. Well, I take the, I snickling, take his plays, you see. I play the drum till I play the drum. Play, play all kinds. Then a piece you can call. Write a piece. Settlement piece. D-d-d-d-d-d-d-d-d-d-d-d-d-d-d-d-d-d-d-d-d-d-d-d-d-d-d-d-d-d-d-d-d-d-d-d-d-d-d-d-d-d-d-d-d-d-d-d-d-d-d-d-d-d-d-d-d-d-d-d-d-d-d-d-d-d-d-d-d-d-d-d-d-d-d-d-d-d-d-d-d-d-d-d-d-d-d-d-d-d-d-d-d-d-d-d-d-d-d-d-d-d-d-d-d-d-d-d-d-d-d boom dear Boop Boop I said, pick it up now. You see that? That's out. I used to be on with all of them. Then I said, I don't know nothing about them. Now when you write to Louis, tell Louis harder for me.

Tell Louis I still, tell Louis I still, tell him that I ain't behind the whoop parade, but I still like to see him back here. Yeah man, there ain't no parades, nothing you can call, I don't know nothing about.
